## Screens, apps and children's reading

In 2025, more than one in five UK 8- to 18-year-olds read fiction on a screen at least monthly [@pictonTrendsChildrenYoung2026].

```{=typst}
#linked-image("figures/evidence.svg", "figures/evidence-links.json")
```

::: {.caption}
Italic rows give findings that cannot be placed on this scale.
:::

::: {.takeaway}
Plain screens cost about 0.2 SD of comprehension, with no clear cost for narratives. Add-ons help when they serve the story, and ed-tech gains shrink on standardised tests.
:::

### Where the research has looked

Research on children's digital reading has studied devices and add-ons far more than the language of the text or log data.

```{=typst}
#image("figures/scopus.svg")
```

::: {.caption}
Scopus records, counted with the scopusflow package [@bernabeuScopusflowCRAN2026]. `r n_both` of the `r n_digital` records fell under both green topics, and we found no meta-analysis of generative AI and children's reading.
:::

```{=typst}
],

#kicker[What we will test]
#question[Using _Let's Story_ reading logs in 18 languages, we test whether text features that slow or speed reading in the laboratory do the same in everyday app use.]
```

## *Let's Story*: AI stories, logged at scale

In this app feature, a child picks a hero, companion, setting, plot and theme. A generative model then writes the story [@ratnerDidRobotWrite2025]. In its first month, *Let's Story* logged 419,700 sessions [@ratnerProductiveStruggleChildrens2026].

## Six registered hypotheses

```{=typst}
#image("figures/model.svg")
```

## Precision comes from stories, not sessions

```{=typst}
#image("figures/precision.svg")
```

::: {.caption}
Chance of showing that a small effect (0.10 SD) is more than negligible, simulated with the pilotr package [@bernabeuPilotrCRAN2026]. A main effect needs `r req$main_lo`–`r req$main_hi` distinct stories, or about `r req$bf_main` under the stricter `#box[Bayes-factor]`{=typst} rule.
:::

::: {.takeaway}
Effects that hold in the app could inform how AI stories are pitched to each age band, though faster reading is not better understanding. Effects that fade may reflect home reading conditions or the measure as much as the theory.
:::
